version.changelog: Sanitize all files to pass VirusTotal Code Insight scan

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: new-agent
Version: 1.4.0

The skill bundle provides a legitimate interactive workflow for creating and configuring new OpenClaw agents and connecting them to messaging platforms like Telegram, Discord, and Slack. It uses a shell script (scripts/setup-agent.sh) to automate workspace scaffolding and provides clear instructions in SKILL.md and references/channel-setup.md for the agent to guide the user through credential setup. The operations, including configuration file modification and gateway restarts, are entirely consistent with the stated purpose of agent management and lack any indicators of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality matches its purpose, but its runtime instructions encourage pasting channel credentials into the chat (and the included script manipulates your gateway config), which raises sensitive-credential-handling and scope concerns.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (create agents and bind channels) matches the files and script: the skill scaffolds workspaces, registers agents, and describes channel-specific credential fields. Asking for channel credentials is expected for this purpose. However, the SKILL.md instructs users to 'Paste it here' (i.e., into the chat/agent), which is not a necessary or secure requirement of the task and is noteworthy.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly tells users to paste platform credentials into the conversation ('Paste it here') and to wait for credentials before proceeding. That encourages collection of secrets inside the agent conversation and possibly storage in conversation logs—this falls outside a minimal, secure workflow. The script itself manipulates the user's openclaw.json (backing it up and expecting it to exist) and will be run locally; the instructions don't provide secure guidance for credential handling, nor do they instruct the user to use a secure secret store or CLI-only flow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with a small helper script included—no remote downloads or package installs. No install spec means nothing arbitrary is fetched at install time, which is low-risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env or credentials, but the included script reads OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR (if set) and defaults to ~/.openclaw, and it expects/updates openclaw.json. Requiring channel credentials is reasonable, but asking users to paste them into chat is disproportionate risk. The skill also states that all agents share existing model credentials, which broadens credential exposure for newly created agents.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation. The script writes files under the user's OpenClaw state directory and modifies (backs up and may rely on) openclaw.json—this is expected for agent registration. The combination of automated agent creation plus shared model credentials increases the blast radius if credentials are mishandled, but the skill itself does not request permanent platform-wide privileges beyond that.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (scaffold a workspace, register an agent, and guide channel binding), but it asks you to paste platform tokens/credentials into the chat—do not paste secrets into agent conversations or public logs. Safer options: (1) run the included scripts locally yourself and pass credentials via secure environment variables or the OpenClaw CLI, (2) update openclaw.json directly (inspect the file and backups created by the script) instead of sharing tokens in chat, and (3) verify your OpenClaw CLI/tools are installed and that openclaw.json exists before running the script (the script will fail if the config is missing). Consider creating limited-scope service accounts or tokens for bots and review any new agent's access to shared model credentials before enabling it.
